name: Mario Diaz-Balart

items.text: In June 2025, Spain's El País published recordings of Colombia's former foreign minister, Álvaro Leyva. He was heard discussing a plan to remove President Gustavo Petro with help from US congressmen, and named Díaz-Balart. Díaz-Balart called the claims "falsehoods and inventions" and "baseless." Colombian prosecutors opened an investigation into the plot.
items.why: Under foreign ties, the only link to him is Leyva's own account on tape, and he denies it; no payment, finding or wrongdoing by him was found.
Being noncommittal before voting yes on a bill (Nov 18, 2025, 427-1, with every Florida House member in favor) is an ordinary vote and stance, not conduct that bears on any criterion.

for_review: Nothing was found on the owner's named sites (alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com); the one search for them returned nothing relevant. Item 1: I could not open the AP/Gazette Xtra article (fetch failed) or El País itself. The recordings' content comes from Colombia Reports and ColombiaOne. A person should confirm whether Colombian prosecutors ever named Díaz-Balart in their investigation. Item 2: the Wikipedia claim that he voted yes only after Trump weighed in was not confirmed by any Local10 or Miami New Times piece I could open. I only saw the House Roll Call result in a search snippet and did not open it, but the Florida Politics snippet says every Florida House member voted yes. Attendance and AIPAC-related items were not weighed, per instructions.
